title: Local dimension formula with generic components through a point
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a locally finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with $S$ locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. For a point $x\in X$ put $s=f(x)$, and write $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $\mathcal O_{S,s}$ for the stalks of the structure sheaves [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], with ring Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $G_x$ be the set of generic points [def-sc-generic-point] of the irreducible components of $X$ containing $x$ [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Then $G_x$ is finite and nonempty, the transcendence degrees $t_\xi=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(\xi))}\kappa(\xi)$ for $\xi\in G_x$ and $t_x=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(x)$ are finite nonnegative integers [def-weil-residue-field, def-kun-transcendence-degree], and, putting $E_x=\max_{\xi\in G_x}t_\xi$, one has
$$\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}+t_x\leq\dim\mathcal O_{S,s}+E_x.$$
No irreducibility, reducedness, dominance, universal catenarity, quasi-compactness, or separatedness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0BAE, lemma-dimension-formula-general: local dimension inequality, in the equivalent form with the nonnegative residue transcendence degree on the left; its proof identifies the finitely many components through x.

proof.text: Choose affine opens $s\in V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$ and $x\in U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$. The scheme axiom gives these neighbourhoods. By [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth], $A$ is Noetherian; by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], the induced map $\varphi:A\to B$ is of finite type. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes $B$ Noetherian. Write $\mathfrak q\subset B$ for $x$ and $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)\subset A$ for $s$, using the point identification of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points].

source.place: Tag 0BAE, lemma-dimension-formula-general, proof; affine realization of the reduced components and their image closures.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], the local rings at $x,s$ are $B_{\mathfrak q},A_{\mathfrak p}$. The localization compatibility in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-stalk-localization] identifies their map with $a/u\mapsto\varphi(a)/\varphi(u)$. Taking quotients by their maximal ideals identifies the residue fields with $\operatorname{Frac}(B/\mathfrak q)$ and $\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p)$, compatibly with this same map: the class of $b/u$ goes to $\bar b/\bar u$, and every nonzero denominator modulo $\mathfrak q$ (respectively $\mathfrak p$) is represented by an element outside that prime. The same description applies to every point of these affine charts.

source.place: Tag 0BAE, lemma-dimension-formula-general, proof; affine realization of the reduced components and their image closures.

proof.text: The components of $U$ are $V(\mathfrak q_i)$ for the minimal primes of $B$, by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes]. Their points $\mathfrak q_i$ are their unique generic points, since the closure of a prime $P$ in a spectrum is $V(P)$ and $V(P)=V(Q)$ for primes forces $P=Q$. Components of $X$ meeting $U$ restrict injectively to components of $U$ by [lem-sc-components-open-injection]. Conversely, the closure in $X$ of a component $D$ of $U$ is a component of $X$: any larger irreducible closed $C$ has $C\cap U=D$ by maximality in $U$, and a nonempty open subset of an irreducible space is dense, so $C=\overline D$. Its generic point is the point $\mathfrak q_i$ of $D$. Thus $G_x$ identifies exactly with the minimal primes $\mathfrak q_i\subseteq\mathfrak q$. This set is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes] and nonempty by [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime] applied to $0\subseteq\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Tag 0BAE, lemma-dimension-formula-general, proof; affine realization of the reduced components and their image closures.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-residue-field-extension-finitely-generated] to $\varphi$ at $\mathfrak q$, and at each of the finitely many $\mathfrak q_i\subseteq\mathfrak q$. Step 2 identifies its field maps with the maps in the statement, including those at $\xi_i=\mathfrak q_i$. Each extension has a finite transcendence basis by [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-generated-field-finite-transcendence-basis]. By the definition of transcendence degree, its value is the finite cardinality of that basis, hence a nonnegative integer. Therefore all $t_x,t_{\xi_i}$ are finite and the maximum $E_x$ exists.

source.place: Tag 0BAE, lemma-dimension-formula-general, proof; affine realization of the reduced components and their image closures.

proof.text: Fix one of these $\mathfrak q_i$ and put $\mathfrak p_i=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q_i)\subseteq\mathfrak p$. Set $Y_i=\operatorname{Spec}(B/\mathfrak q_i)$ and $Z_i=\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak p_i)$. The map $A/\mathfrak p_i\to B/\mathfrak q_i$ is injective, and the images of any finite algebra-generating set of $B/A$ generate its target. Both quotient rings are domains, so [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field] makes both schemes integral with generic point $(0)$. This map sends the generic point of $Y_i$ to that of $Z_i$, so it is dominant. It is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-pointwise-criterion], using the displayed affine pair at every point; its base is locally Noetherian, since $A/\mathfrak p_i$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] (a quotient is generated by the empty family as an $A$-algebra). The points $y_i=\mathfrak q/\mathfrak q_i$, $z_i=\mathfrak p/\mathfrak p_i$ map to each other.

source.place: Tag 0BAE, lemma-dimension-formula-general, proof; affine realization of the reduced components and their image closures.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field](1) to identify $\mathcal O_{Y_i,y_i}=B_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q_iB_{\mathfrak q}$ and $\mathcal O_{Z_i,z_i}=A_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak p_iA_{\mathfrak p}$. Their residue fields are those of $x,s$: quotienting further by $\mathfrak qB_{\mathfrak q}$ and $\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$ gives exactly the same fields. By clause (2) of the same spectrum lemma, their function fields are $\operatorname{Frac}(B/\mathfrak q_i)$ and $\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p_i)$, namely $\kappa(\xi_i)$ and $\kappa(f(\xi_i))$. All maps are induced by $\varphi$; on fractions they send $\bar a/\bar u$ to $\overline{\varphi(a)}/\overline{\varphi(u)}$. Thus the residue and generic transcendence degrees for $Y_i\to Z_i$ are exactly $t_x$ and $t_{\xi_i}$.

source.place: Tag 0BAE, lemma-dimension-formula-general, proof; affine realization of the reduced components and their image closures.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-local-dimension-formula] to $Y_i\to Z_i$ and $y_i$. Step 5 has verified integrality, dominance, local finite type and the locally Noetherian base; no catenarity hypothesis is needed for this inequality. Substituting the identifications of Step 6 yields $$\dim(B_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q_iB_{\mathfrak q})+t_x\leq\dim(A_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak p_iA_{\mathfrak p})+t_{\xi_i}.$$ This holds for every $\mathfrak q_i\subseteq\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Tag 0BAE, lemma-dimension-formula-general, proof; affine realization of the reduced components and their image closures.

proof.text: For any ring $R$ and ideal $I$, prime chains of $R/I$ inject into those of $R$, with the same lengths: send each prime to its inverse image; the inverse on primes containing $I$ is $P\mapsto P/I$, which is prime because $(R/I)/(P/I)=R/P$ is a domain. Thus $\dim(A_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak p_iA_{\mathfrak p})\leq\dim A_{\mathfrak p}$. Also $$\dim B_{\mathfrak q}=\max_i\dim(B_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak q_iB_{\mathfrak q}).$$ Indeed every finite prime chain in $B_{\mathfrak q}$ contracts to a strict chain in $B$ ending below $\mathfrak q$ by [lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization]. Its first prime contains a minimal prime $\mathfrak q_i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime]; this $i$ is in our list. The chain therefore descends to the quotient by $\mathfrak q_iB_{\mathfrak q}$ with its length unchanged. Conversely every chain in any such quotient lifts to $B_{\mathfrak q}$. Taking suprema gives the equality, since the list is finite and nonempty.

source.place: Tag 0BAE, lemma-dimension-formula-general, proof; affine realization of the reduced components and their image closures.

proof.text: In Step 7 bound the target quotient dimension by $\dim A_{\mathfrak p}$ using Step 8, and bound $t_{\xi_i}$ by $E_x$ using its definition. Taking the maximum over the nonempty finite list and using Step 8 gives $$\dim B_{\mathfrak q}+t_x\leq\dim A_{\mathfrak p}+E_x.$$ Step 2 identifies these with the asserted local dimensions. Steps 3--4 gave precisely the other clauses. All choices were affine neighbourhoods of the prescribed points; no global finiteness or separation, nor reducedness or irreducibility of $X,S$, was used.

lean.statement: theorem local_dimension_formula_generic_components {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [IsLocallyNoetherian S] (x : X) : ∃ (G : Finset X) (tx : ℕ) (t : X → ℕ), (∀ ξ : X, ξ ∈ G ↔ ∃ Z ∈ irreducibleComponents X, x ∈ Z ∧ IsGenericPoint ξ Z) ∧ G.Nonempty ∧ @Algebra.trdeg (S.residueField (f x)) (X.residueField x) _ _ (f.residueFieldMap x).hom.toAlgebra = (tx : Cardinal) ∧ (∀ ξ ∈ G, @Algebra.trdeg (S.residueField (f ξ)) (X.residueField ξ) _ _ (f.residueFieldMap ξ).hom.toAlgebra = (t ξ : Cardinal)) ∧ ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x) + (tx : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ ringKrullDim (S.presheaf.stalk (f x)) + ((G.sup t : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞)
